search_strategy: Two phases. First, Mattermost API keyword search (terms like 'ledger', 'CHECKPOINT_REASONS', 'canonical_reasons', 'min_lr_ratio', 'current_batch', 'CheckpointInfo') dumped to /tmp/mm_*.txt/grep hits — this surfaces individual matching MESSAGES, not full threads, so when the keyword only appears in one side of an exchange (typically the asker's line), the answer is silently missed even though the pointer sheet would mark the remark 'found' because the question line hit. Second, once a topic was identified as rich, the agent dumped whole channel histories to /tmp/c_<channel>.txt (~10k messages total, step ~35-36) and either grepped those files for follow-up terms or explicitly printed line ranges (e.g. 'Print releases 505-600 and 300-345', line 4162) to read full exchanges. This second technique worked well (captures nearly all of r2's herrings/reversals, most of r1's scope/exclusions/observability clues) but was undermined at least twice by a small terminal-scrollback window: multi-range prints only left the LAST range visible in 'Current Terminal Screen', so a range containing a needed reply (#releases 515-560, carrying r1.l17's reason-merge instruction) was requested but never actually seen. The agent never fetched BookStack wiki comments or mail at all for this task (all 47 remarks are chat-only per the plant record, so this cost nothing here). No pipeline/wiki/mail search was needed since the corpus for g11 is 100% Mattermost.
end_reason: Run completed normally: PR 730 merged to main (via local --no-ff after Gitea's merge API returned HTTP 500), CI green on cd5475b, 168 finetune tests pass. reward=0.8889 reflects 8/9 facts; the only miss is g11.r1.failure_behavior's reason-merge-on-repeat-save requirement.
notable: Root cause of the only lost fact is a genuine near-miss, not a misread: g11.r1.l17's payload (the specific merge-both-reason-tuples instruction) never reached the agent's context, due to a combination of keyword-search-hits-only-one-side-of-a-thread and a scrolled-past explicit follow-up read (line 4162).

The same failure pattern (keyword search surfaces the question, not the answer) also hit g11.r2.say19 (line 5378), but that fact (r2.exclusions_or_crossover) was saved by redundant coverage from r2.l14/l15.
All 4 herrings were correctly identified and their reversals correctly followed in the shipped code — no herring-following occurred anywhere in this run.

The agent's own final Analysis (line 9035) explicitly states the (incomplete) rule it implemented: 'dedupe against the last row only' — confirming the gap was in what it believed, consistent with what it actually read (l16/rev1's 'replace' language) rather than a slip between correct belief and incorrect code.

Gitea's PR-merge API returned HTTP 500 for all three merge methods citing an unrelated branch; the agent worked around it with a local --no-ff merge + push and documented this on the PR (lines 8578-8873) — unrelated to fact grading but worth flagging as a harness quirk for other g11 runs.
